review_note: English content written and checked against public guidance from the cited official sources.

categories.title: UPI payment scams
categories.summary: A fraudster talks you into scanning a QR code or entering your UPI PIN so that money leaves your account, usually while pretending to send you money.
categories.example: I am from the bank. Your refund is stuck. Scan this QR code and enter your UPI PIN to receive the amount.
warning_signs: You are asked to scan a QR code or enter your PIN to receive money
An unexpected collect request appears in your UPI app
The caller claims to be bank staff, a merchant or a refund agent
You are told the request expires in a few minutes
prevention: A UPI PIN sends money. It is never needed to receive money
Reject collect requests you did not expect, even for small amounts
Check the payee name in your own app before approving anything
checklist: Do not scan a QR code to receive a payment
Reject the request and check your balance in the official app
If money was taken, call 1930 and report at cybercrime.gov.in

categories.title: OTP and verification-code scams
categories.summary: Anyone who learns your one-time password can finish a transaction or reset your account. No genuine bank, company or government office ever asks you to share it.
categories.example: Your KYC expires today. Share the OTP we just sent to keep your account active.
warning_signs: Someone asks for an OTP, CVV, PIN or password
A link is provided to 'verify' or 'reactivate' the account
The caller already knows part of your account or card number
A deadline is used to stop you thinking
prevention: Never share an OTP, CVV, PIN or password with anyone
No bank employee needs your OTP to help you
Open the bank app yourself instead of using a link in a message
checklist: Hang up or stop replying
Call the number printed on your card or passbook
Report the message to cybercrime.gov.in

categories.title: Phishing links and fake apps
categories.summary: Messages that look like a bank, courier, electricity board or government notice push you to a look-alike website or an APK file that steals credentials.
categories.example: Your electricity connection will be disconnected tonight. Update your details here: http://kseb-bill-update.example
warning_signs: Shortened or misspelled web addresses
A request to install an APK file from outside an app store
The page asks for card details, net-banking credentials or an OTP
Threats of disconnection, suspension or legal action
prevention: Type the official website address yourself instead of tapping a link
Check the domain carefully, including spellings and endings
Install apps only from the official app stores
checklist: Do not open the link
Check the bill or account in the official app
Forward the message to cybercrime.gov.in and delete it

categories.title: Fake job and task scams
categories.summary: Scammers advertise easy work-from-home jobs, then ask for a registration or joining fee, or use 'task' jobs to move stolen money through your account.
categories.example: Earn Rs 3,000 daily from home. Pay Rs 500 registration to start immediately. No interview needed.
warning_signs: You must pay a fee to get a job
No interview and no written offer letter
Communication only through WhatsApp or Telegram
Very high pay for simple tasks such as liking videos
You are asked to receive money and forward it elsewhere
prevention: Legitimate employers do not charge candidates
Verify the company on its official website and on LinkedIn
Never let anyone route money through your bank account
checklist: Stop paying any 'registration' or 'training' fee
Collect the chat, number and payment details
Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930

categories.title: Lottery and prize scams
categories.summary: You are told you won a lottery or draw you never entered. To release the prize you must pay tax, a processing fee or share account details.
categories.example: Congratulations! Your number won Rs 25,00,000 in the lucky draw. Pay Rs 6,500 processing fee to receive the prize.
warning_signs: A prize from a draw you never entered
A fee, tax or courier charge must be paid first
Requests for bank details, Aadhaar or an OTP
A short deadline before the 'prize expires'
prevention: You cannot win a lottery you did not enter
Never pay money to receive money
Genuine prizes do not require an OTP or your PIN
checklist: Do not pay any fee
Do not share identity or bank documents
Report and block the sender

categories.title: Investment and trading scams
categories.summary: Guaranteed-return schemes, fake trading apps and 'double your money' groups take deposits, show fake profits, then block withdrawals.
categories.example: Join our VIP trading group. Guaranteed 30% monthly return. Deposit Rs 10,000 today and withdraw anytime.
warning_signs: Returns are described as guaranteed or risk-free
The adviser is not registered with SEBI
The app is shared as a link or APK, not through an app store
Withdrawals are blocked until you pay more 'tax' or 'fees'
Celebrity videos endorse the scheme
prevention: Check the adviser's SEBI registration number
Treat guaranteed high returns as a warning sign, not an offer
Keep evidence of every transfer
checklist: Do not deposit more money
Try a small withdrawal early to test the platform
Report to cybercrime.gov.in and, for unauthorised schemes, to RBI Sachet

categories.title: Bank impersonation and KYC fraud
categories.summary: Callers pose as bank security staff, RBI or the police, claim your account is involved in crime, and ask you to move money to a 'safe account'.
categories.example: This is bank security. Your account is linked to money laundering. Transfer your balance to this RBI safe account to protect it.
warning_signs: Instructions to move money to a 'safe', 'escrow' or 'government' account
Threats of arrest, account freeze or legal action
A request to install a screen-sharing or remote-access app
Caller ID that looks like the bank's number
Requests for card details, PIN or OTP
prevention: No bank or police officer asks you to transfer money to a safe account
End the call and dial the number on your card or passbook
Never install remote-access apps at a caller's request
checklist: Hang up immediately
Check your account in the official app
Call 1930 and report at cybercrime.gov.in if money moved
